predecessors.name: Communist Party of Burma
predecessors.text: Kokang, 'its total land area is around 1,895 square kilometers': a 25 km circle at Laukkai cut to Shan State

ledger.x: 1989: the MNDAA is formed on 12 March by Pheung Kya-shin, the head of the CPB's Kokang branch, 'the first one to sign a ceasefire agreement with the Burmese government'.
2015: the MNDAA tries to retake Kokang.
2024: the contest over Kokang closes with the fall of Laukkai on 5 January.
2024: the MNDAA takes Lashio in early August, the largest town in northern Shan State; it withdrew in April 2025 under a ceasefire deal.

wars.name: 2009 Kokang incident
wars.outcome: The Tatmadaw occupied Laukkai on 24 August 2009 and the MNDAA lost control of Kokang.

wars.name: 2015 Kokang offensive
wars.outcome: The MNDAA tried to retake Kokang on 9 February 2015; martial law followed on 17 February; no territorial result on the pages.

wars.name: Operation 1027 (Kokang and Lashio fronts)
wars.outcome: Laukkai fell on 5 January 2024; the MNDAA began surrounding Lashio on 25 June 2024 and took it in early August 2024 and withdrew in April 2025.

certainty.note: Special-region and rebel-held lines are unpublished; the circles are the researcher's placement.
